proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) and put \(\delta=1/2-\eta\).  We first construct one interior point of the asserted family.  Let
\[
 b(z)=c_b\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\},
 \qquad m_2=\int_{-1}^1z^2b(z)\,dz,
\]
where \(c_b\) normalizes the density.  Symmetry gives \(\mathbb E Z=0\), and strict positivity on \((-1,1)\) gives \(0<m_2<1\).  Let
\[
 \beta(t)=c_\beta\exp\{-1/[t(1-t)]\}\mathbf 1\{0<t<1\},
 \qquad L=3,
\]
with \(c_\beta\) again chosen to give integral one.  Define the strictly positive numbers
\[
 e_\eta=\frac{\delta m_2}{64L^2},\qquad
 v_\eta=L^2e_\eta(1-e_\eta),\qquad
 B_\eta=\frac{\delta v_\eta}{256},
\]
and then
\[
 h_\eta=\sqrt{B_\eta/8},
 \qquad \tau_\eta=\frac{B_\eta}{2L^2}.
\]
Because \(0<\delta<1/2\), \(0<m_2<1\), and \(L=3\), these choices satisfy \(0<e_\eta<1/2\), \(0<h_\eta<1/4\), and \(0<\tau_\eta<1\).  On \([0,L]\), set
\[
 p_\eta(x)=(1-\tau_\eta)
 \left\{(1-e_\eta)h_\eta^{-1}\beta(x/h_\eta)
 +e_\eta h_\eta^{-1}\beta((L-x)/h_\eta)\right\}
 +\frac{\tau_\eta}{L}. \tag{15}
\]
The bump terms in (15) are zero off their indicated endpoint bands.  Let \(X\) have density \(p_\eta\), let \(N\) have density \(b\), take \(X\perp N\), and set
\[
 Y=X+N. \tag{16}
\]
The node domains are \([0,L]\) and \([-1,L+1]\), and the generating graph is \(X\to Y\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), including its identification restriction.  The functions \(b\), \(\beta\), and \(p_\eta\) are \(C^\infty\) on their relative interiors; \(b\) is positive on \((-1,1)\), and the bridge term makes \(p_\eta\) positive on all of \((0,L)\).  Equation (16) has a nonconstant \(C^\infty\) mechanism, independent innovations, and
\[
 [0,L]+[-1,1]=[-1,L+1],
\]
so Assumptions \(\ref{ass:anm-independence}\), \(\ref{ass:smooth-mechanisms}\), \(\ref{ass:smooth-positive-densities}\), \(\ref{ass:support-closure}\), and \(\ref{ass:causal-minimality}\) hold.  The root support and every bivariate conditional-support fiber have connected relative interior.  Both variances are positive, so Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) holds for this model with any positive lower bound smaller than their minimum.

It remains to check the Condition 19 configuration.  Write \(\xi=\log p_\eta\), \(\nu=\log b\), and
\[
 \Lambda(x,y)=\xi(x)+\nu(y-x)
\]
on the interior of the joint support.  If a reverse additive-noise representation existed locally, then for some functions \(g\), \(r\), and \(s\) its log-density would have the form
\[
 \Lambda(x,y)=r(x-g(y))+s(y).
\]
At points where \(\Lambda_{xx}\ne0\), direct differentiation would give
\[
 \frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}=-g'(y),
 \qquad
 \partial_x\left(\frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}\right)=0. \tag{17}
\]
Thus failure of (17) is precisely the required local differential obstruction.  For the forward density,
\[
 \Lambda_{xx}=\xi''(x)+\nu''(y-x),
 \qquad \Lambda_{xy}=-\nu''(y-x).
\]
Since \(b\) is symmetric, \(\nu'''(0)=0\), while direct differentiation of \(\nu(z)=\log c_b-1/(1-z^2)\) gives \(\nu''(0)=-2\ne0\).  Hence at \(y=x\), whenever the denominator is nonzero,
\[
 \partial_x\left(\frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}\right)
 =\frac{\nu''(0)\xi'''(x)}{\{\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)\}^2}. \tag{18}
\]
There exists \(x\in(0,h_\eta)\) for which the right side of (18) is nonzero.  Indeed, if \(\xi'''\) vanished throughout \((0,h_\eta)\), then \(\xi\) would be quadratic there.  Flatness of the bump at \(h_\eta\) gives \(\xi'(h_\eta-)=\xi''(h_\eta-)=0\), forcing that quadratic to be constant, contrary to the nonconstant bump in (15).  Thus the open set \(\{x:\xi'''(x)\ne0\}\) is nonempty.  The identity \(\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)=0\) cannot hold throughout any component of that open set, because differentiating it would give \(\xi'''=0\).  This proves the assertion.  Continuity makes (18) nonzero on an interior open patch.  Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) therefore holds, as does Assumption \(\ref{ass:connected-support-fibers}\).  The constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), and Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies its labelled graph as \(X\to Y\).

We next bound the two correlation ratios.  Couple \(X\) to \(X_0\in\{0,L\}\) as follows.  On the two bump components use their corresponding endpoint; on the bridge component draw \(X_0=L\) with probability \(e_\eta\), independently of the bridge draw, and otherwise take \(X_0=0\).  Then \(\mathbb P(X_0=L)=e_\eta\), \(\operatorname{Var}(X_0)=v_\eta\), and
\[
 \mathbb E(X-X_0)^2
 \le h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta
 =\frac{5B_\eta}{8}<B_\eta. \tag{19}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality in \(L^2\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, yields
\[
 \left|\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)}-\sqrt{v_\eta}\right|
 \le \left\|(X-\mathbb EX)-(X_0-\mathbb EX_0)\right\|_2
 \le2\|X-X_0\|_2<2\sqrt{B_\eta}. \tag{20}
\]
Since \(B_\eta/v_\eta=\delta/256<1/512\), (20) implies the convenient bounds
\[
 \frac12v_\eta<\operatorname{Var}(X)<2v_\eta. \tag{21}
\]
Independence and \(\mathbb EN=0\) give \(\mathbb E[Y\mid X]=X\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2\).  Definitions \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) and \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\), followed by (21), therefore give
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2}
 \le\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{m_2}
 <\frac{2v_\eta}{m_2}
 \le\frac{2L^2e_\eta}{m_2}
 =\frac{\delta}{32}. \tag{22}
\]

For the reverse prediction problem, use
\[
 \widehat X(Y)=0\quad\text{if }Y<L/2,
 \qquad
 \widehat X(Y)=L\quad\text{if }Y\ge L/2.
\]
Because \(h_\eta<1/4\) and the noise support is \([-1,1]\), this rule classifies both bump components correctly.  Its squared error is at most \(h_\eta^2\) on them and at most \(L^2\) on the bridge.  Conditional-mean optimality in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\), (19), and (21) imply
\[
 R_{X,\{Y\}}=\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)
 \le h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta<B_\eta,
\]
and consequently
\[
 1-q(X,\{Y\})
 =\frac{R_{X,\{Y\}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 <\frac{2B_\eta}{v_\eta}
 =\frac{\delta}{128}. \tag{23}
\]
Combining (22) and (23),
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac12-\frac{\delta}{256}-\frac{\delta}{32}
 =\frac12-\frac{9\delta}{256}
 >\frac12-\delta=\eta. \tag{24}
\]

We now thicken the construction by primitive strict inequalities.  This also makes the meaning of relative openness explicit.  On each fixed graph stratum, transport every compact interval affinely to a reference interval and use the product of: Euclidean convergence of support endpoints, uniform \(C^1\) and compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of mechanisms, and \(L^1\) plus compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of innovation densities.  Give the finitely many graph strata the discrete topology.  This is the structural topology used below.

For a two-node model in the \(X\to Y\) stratum, write the root and child-noise support intervals as \([a,b]\) and \([c,d]\), write the mechanism as \(g\), and put \(r_\eta=2h_\eta\).  Define the endpoint bands
\[
 A_0=[a,a+r_\eta],\qquad A_1=[b-r_\eta,b],
\]
whenever \(b-a>2r_\eta\), and define
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cl}}=r_\eta^2+(b-a)^2
 \mathbb P\{X\notin A_0\cup A_1\}. \tag{25}
\]
Let \(\mathcal U_\eta\) consist of the members of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) in this stratum for which
\[
 \inf_{x\in[a,b]}g'(x)>0, \tag{26}
\]
\[
 \sup_{x\in A_0}g(x)+d
 <\inf_{x\in A_1}g(x)+c, \tag{27}
\]
\[
 \frac{B_{\mathrm{cl}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}<\frac{\delta}{16}, \tag{28}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{29}
\]
These conditions expose the variables and all divisions: the denominators in (28) and (29) are positive by Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\), and child-noise variance is positive because its density is positive on a nondegenerate interval.

The set \(\mathcal U_\eta\) is relatively open.  Conditions (26)--(29) are strict; extrema in (26)--(27), probabilities and variances in (25), (28), and (29), and their positive-denominator ratios are continuous in the stated topology.  At the reference model (15)--(16), the mass outside \([0,2h_\eta]\cup[L-2h_\eta,L]\) is at most \(\tau_\eta\), so
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cl}}\le4h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta=B_\eta.
\]
Equations (21)--(22) imply (28)--(29).  Moreover, (26) holds with derivative one, and (27) follows from
\[
 2h_\eta+1<L-2h_\eta-1,
\]
which is equivalent to \(h_\eta<1/4\).  Thus the reference law lies in \(\mathcal U_\eta\), proving that this relatively open set is nonempty.

Every law in \(\mathcal U_\eta\) obeys the desired strict margin by the same two elementary risk bounds, without appealing to continuity of the score.  Choose a threshold strictly between the two sides of (27), predict \(a\) below it and \(b\) above it.  On \(A_0\cup A_1\) the squared error is at most \(r_\eta^2\), and outside it the squared error is at most \((b-a)^2\).  Hence (25), conditional-mean optimality, and (28) give
\[
 1-q(X,\{Y\})
 =\frac{R_{X,\{Y\}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 \le\frac{B_{\mathrm{cl}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{30}
\]
By independent additive noise,
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{31}
\]
Equations (30)--(31) yield
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac12-\frac{\delta}{32}-\frac{\delta}{16}
 =\frac12-\frac{3\delta}{32}>\eta. \tag{32}
\]

Reverse residual dependence holds at every point of \(\mathcal U_\eta\) by support geometry, not by continuity of an independence indicator.  Positivity of the two densities on their interval interiors and strict increase in (26) imply that, for
\[
 y\in\bigl(g(a)+c,\,\min\{g(a)+d,g(b)+c\}\bigr),
\]
an interval of positive \(P_Y\)-measure, the relative interior of the conditional support is
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(X\mid Y=y)^\circ
 =\bigl(a,g^{-1}(y-c)\bigr). \tag{33}
\]
Its diameter \(g^{-1}(y-c)-a\) is strictly increasing in \(y\).  Subtracting \(\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\) translates (33) and does not alter its diameter.  If \(X-\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\) were independent of \(Y\), its regular conditional distribution, hence its closed support and support diameter, would be the same for \(P_Y\)-almost every \(y\), contradicting (33).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\) and Definition \(\ref{def:hsic}\) therefore give
\[
 H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0 \tag{34}
\]
throughout \(\mathcal U_\eta\).  No continuity at the independence boundary is asserted or needed.

The family genuinely lies in the broad nonlinear-ANM regime.  For example, replace the identity mechanism at the reference point by
\[
 g_s(x)=x+s x(L-x).
\]
For every sufficiently small nonzero \(s\), this mechanism is non-affine and \(C^3\), maps \([0,L]\) monotonically onto itself, preserves (26)--(29), and preserves the strict differential failure (18) by compact-open \(C^3\) continuity.  Hence these perturbations remain in \(\mathcal U_\eta\cap\mathcal M_0(2)\).  The affine mechanisms form a closed subset in the declared structural topology: if \(g_m(x)=a_mx+b_m\) converges in uniform \(C^1\), then \(g_m'\) converges uniformly to \(g'\), and because every \(g_m'\) is constant, \(g'\) is constant, so \(g\) is affine.  Therefore the complement of the affine mechanisms is relatively open.  Intersecting that complement with \(\mathcal U_\eta\) gives the asserted nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily.

It remains to translate the inequalities into the GENE landscape.  In the causal order \((X,Y)\), the residual of \(Y\) on \(X\) is \(N-\mathbb EN\), independent of \(X\), so Definitions \(\ref{def:hsic}\)--\(\ref{def:gene-score}\) give
\[
 S_P(X,Y)=q(Y,\{X\}). \tag{35}
\]
In the reverse order, (34) makes the dependence count equal to one, and therefore
\[
 S_P(Y,X)=\frac12q(X,\{Y\}). \tag{36}
\]
By (32), (36) is strictly larger than (35).  There are only two labelled orders, so \((Y,X)\) is the unique global maximizer and hence the unique insertion-local maximizer, even though Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies \(X\to Y\) for every member of \(\mathcal U_\eta\).

Finally, Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) gives \(0\le q\le1\).  Consequently every nondegenerate bivariate law satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})\le\frac12. \tag{37}
\]
For every \(\eta<1/2\), (32) supplies a member of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) with generating graph \(X\to Y\) for which the difference is larger than \(\eta\).  Thus the displayed supremum equals \(1/2\), proving sharpness.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Equip each fixed-graph stratum of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) with the product structural topology given by Euclidean convergence of support endpoints, uniform \(C^1\) and compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of mechanisms after affine transport to fixed reference intervals, and \(L^1\) plus compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of innovation densities, and give the graph strata the discrete topology. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), there is an explicitly parameterized nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal U_\eta\subset\mathcal M_0(2)\), all of whose members have generating graph \(X\to Y\), such that every law in \(\mathcal U_\eta\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})>\eta,
 \qquad H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0.
\]
Thus the wrong order \((Y,X)\) is the unique global maximizer, and hence an insertion-local maximizer, of the exact \(\alpha=1\) population GENE score, although the causal order \(X\to Y\) is identifiable. Moreover, \(\mathcal U_\eta\) contains a nonempty relatively open subfamily having a non-affine child mechanism, and
\[
 \sup\left\{\frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\}):(G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_0(2),\ G_0=(X\to Y)\right\}=\frac12.
\]

The proposed claim records exactly those already-proved conclusions without extending the matching-class success result to any larger class.

proposed.statement:
Equip each fixed-graph stratum of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) with the product structural topology given by Euclidean convergence of support endpoints, uniform \(C^1\) and compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of mechanisms after affine transport to fixed reference intervals, and \(L^1\) plus compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of innovation densities, and give the graph strata the discrete topology. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), there is an explicitly parameterized nonempty relatively open set \(\mathcal U_\eta\subset\mathcal M_0(2)\), all of whose members have generating graph \(X\to Y\), such that every law in \(\mathcal U_\eta\) satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})>\eta,
 \qquad H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0.
\]
Thus the wrong order \((Y,X)\) is the unique global maximizer, and hence an insertion-local maximizer, of the exact \(\alpha=1\) population GENE score, although the causal order \(X\to Y\) is identifiable. Moreover, \(\mathcal U_\eta\) contains a nonempty relatively open subfamily having a non-affine child mechanism, and
\[
 \sup\left\{\frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\}):(G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_0(2),\ G_0=(X\to Y)\right\}=\frac12.
\]
proposed.justification: This theorem certifies that observational ANM identifiability does not by itself control the exact GENE population landscape: a structurally open family can make the unique wrong-order optimum arbitrarily close to the largest score advantage allowed by \(0\le q\le1\).
proposed.gap: The earlier fixed-margin construction did not establish the sharp \(1/2\) boundary or a margin-indexed open family, and treating nonzero HSIC as continuous would have hidden the discontinuity of exact independence.
proposed.consumer: Users of population or high-precision GENE optimization obtain an explicit adversarial family and know that the matching-class success certificate cannot be omitted merely because the underlying ANM is identifiable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened claim directly names the structural primitives in its sharp supremum, so its free-symbol metadata must include those symbols while retaining the existing proof dependencies and result notes.

prose_updates.tldr: For the exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue of GENE Equation (6), a primitive edgewise inequality on support-closed matching-component additive-noise models forces a positive reversal-correcting insertion at every wrong order, so best improvement and independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. This is a certified success region, not a theorem for Li et al.'s full nonlinear class. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), an explicitly parameterized relatively open bivariate family, including a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily, makes the identifiable causal model \(X\to Y\) have the wrong order as its unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer with score advantage strictly greater than \(\eta\); the universal sharp supremum is \(1/2\). Cross-fitted simultaneous bands abstain at unresolved independence labels; on separated labels, \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\), and direct margin inequalities yield the sufficient sample size \(n\gtrsim\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\), with the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\) and no minimax claim. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the stated HSIC separation promise, the set-valued output covers \(G_0\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) even when the width inequalities fail; those inequalities are required only for singleton recovery, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The success certificate is sufficient only on matching-component DAGs and is not an observable necessary-and-sufficient boundary for general GENE landscapes. The sharp bivariate construction proves a margin-indexed relatively open failure region, including a relatively open non-affine subfamily, inside the identifiable nonlinear-ANM class and attains the universal one-half supremum only as a limit; it does not classify the intervening general class. Exact independence remains discontinuous: the population trap handles it pointwise by support geometry throughout its open structural family, while finite-sample inference requires the stated HSIC separation promise and otherwise retains both labels. Under the matching class and that separation promise, simultaneous coverage still gives \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) when the score and HSIC width inequalities fail, but only the width inequalities certify singleton recovery; the compatible-DAG union may then be singleton or multiple. The residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC radius uses the stated nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The displayed sample-size order suppresses fixed regularity constants and is sufficient, not minimax optimal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered population results are a compact-support identification bridge, a matching-subclass insertion-navigation theorem, a six-node strict separation witness, finite-query oracle recovery, a quadratic positive-gain witness, and, for every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), a sharp relatively open bivariate trapped-order family with a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily. The wrong order is the unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer by more than \(\eta\), while the universal supremum of this score advantage is \(1/2\). The matching-subclass theorem does not establish success on Li et al.'s full nonlinear class; the nonlinear witnesses transfer to that class only existentially, and the trap does not contradict Theorem 4.3 because its global-ranking premise fails there. The simultaneous-band theorem gives \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\) on separated labels when \(w_R<\underline v/2\), together with direct sufficient conditions \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the existing HSIC separation promise, \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) remains valid even when those width inequalities fail; singleton recovery requires the inequalities, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple. No minimax rate, observable general-class boundary, or claim against Li et al. Theorem 4.3 is made. The released Sachs workflow remains an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold does not certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference directions do not follow from an observational acyclic ANM alone.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem certifies that observational ANM identifiability does not by itself control the exact GENE population landscape: for every desired margin below the universal one-half boundary, a structurally open family makes the wrong order uniquely optimal.
statement_notes.gap: A fixed-margin witness would not establish the sharp \(1/2\) boundary, a margin-indexed relatively open family, or a relatively open non-affine subfamily; continuity of nonzero HSIC cannot be used because exact independence is discontinuous.
statement_notes.consumer: Users of population or high-precision GENE optimization obtain an explicit sharp adversarial family and know that the matching-class success certificate cannot be omitted merely because the underlying ANM is identifiable.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and let \(\underline v\) be the constant in Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\). Compactness of \(\mathcal X\) supplies a finite bound \(B\) for every coordinate of \(V\) and every clipped residual used below. All constants denoted by \(K\), \(K_R\), or \(K_H\) may depend on \(B\), the fixed fold proportions, the Holder radius, the two design-density bounds, the kernel bounds, and \(L_k\), but not on \(n\), \(\alpha\), or the particular indices \((v,A,u)\).

We first construct the regression fits and record their simultaneous error. Fix \(v\in I\), \(A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\), and put \(m=|A|\). Partition \(\mathcal X_A\) into rectangles of side at most \(h\), use polynomials of total degree at most two on each nonempty rectangle, and clip their values to the coordinate range of \(V_v\). Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a member \(g_h\) of this sieve such that
\[
 \lVert g_h-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_\infty\le K h^3. \tag{1}
\]
There are at most \(K h^{-m}\) polynomial coefficients. The least-squares bound needed here follows directly from the empirical basic inequality. For bounded squared-loss differences, the conditional variance is at most \(K\) times the excess squared-error risk. On a shell whose population excess risk is \(r\), the exponential Markov inequality and a finite-dimensional net for the \(K h^{-m}\) coefficients give an upper probability \(\exp\{-c n r+K h^{-m}\}\). Peeling over dyadic values of \(r\), using (1) as the comparison element, and summing the resulting geometric series therefore gives, for the clipped empirical least-squares fit on a training fold of size proportional to \(n\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left[
 \lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 >K\left\{h^6+\frac{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\right\}
 \right]\le\delta . \tag{2}
\]
Thus (2) uses only boundedness, the two stated smoothness and design conditions, and independent sampling; it requires no unrecorded moment or tail condition.

Take \(h=t_n^{1/(m+6)}\) when \(t_n\le1\), and allocate failure probability proportional to \(\alpha/M_d\). Since \(m\le d-1\),
\[
 t_n^{3/(m+6)}\le t_n^{3/(d+5)}=a_n.
\]
A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions therefore yields, with the allocated simultaneous probability,
\[
 \max_{v,A}\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{3}
\]
When \(t_n>1\), clipping and enlargement of \(K\) give (3) directly because both the response and fitted regression are bounded. Repeating the construction over the fixed number of cross-fitting folds changes only \(K\).

On an evaluation fold independent of a fitted regression, let \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) be the empirical mean of the squared fitted residual. The defining orthogonality of conditional expectation in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) gives, conditionally on the training fold,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}\right]
 =R_{v,A}+\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{4}
\]
The evaluation losses are conditionally independent and bounded. If a centered random variable \(W\) satisfies \(|W|\le b\), convexity of the exponential on \([-b,b]\) gives \(\mathbb E e^{sW}\le e^{s^2b^2/2}\). Exponential Markov optimization followed by a union bound consequently gives a simultaneous evaluation error of at most \(K\sqrt{t_n}\). Combining this fact with (3)--(4) produces intervals centered at \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) that contain every \(R_{v,A}\) and whose common half-width obeys
\[
 w_R\le K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n^2\}
 =K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}. \tag{5}
\]

For the HSIC coordinates, use the bounded, centered order-four V-statistic on the evaluation fold, with the off-fold residuals. Conditional on the training fold, changing one evaluation observation changes this statistic by at most \(K/n\). Exposing the observations one at a time and applying the preceding exponential argument gives deviation \(K\sqrt{t_n}\); terms with repeated indices contribute at most \(K/n\), which is absorbed into that bound. It remains to compare the population HSIC of fitted and true residuals. The population HSIC expansion is a fixed finite sum of expectations of products of bounded kernel factors. Telescope each product at its residual-kernel factor and apply Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\). Cauchy--Schwarz and (3) then give
\[
 \left|H_{\widehat\mu}(v,A,u)-H(v,A,u)\right|
 \le K\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A)-\mu_{v,A}(V_A)\right|
 \le K a_n. \tag{6}
\]
Consequently simultaneous intervals contain all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant HSIC coordinates and satisfy
\[
 w_H\le K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n\}
 =K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}. \tag{7}
\]
The pruning coordinates have the form \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\). Their number is at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\), so the same union bound covers every possibly adaptive pruning query. This replaces \(M_d\) by at most \(2M_d\); because \(M_d/\alpha\ge2\), \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\), and the change is absorbed into \(K_H\). Allocating the preceding failure probabilities so that their sum is at most \(\alpha\) proves the asserted simultaneous coverage and the two band rates.

We next make the score-radius consequence explicit. Work on the simultaneous-coverage event and suppose that the separated decision has fixed each score-relevant dependence indicator at its correct singleton value. Assume \(w_R<\underline v/2\). Write
\[
 y_v=R_{v,\varnothing}=\operatorname{Var}_P(V_v),
 \qquad x_{v,A}=R_{v,A}.
\]
Conditional expectation is the \(L^2(P)\) projection onto the functions of \(V_A\), so Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) and Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) imply
\[
 0\le x_{v,A}\le y_v,
 \qquad y_v\ge\underline v. \tag{8}
\]
Let \(\widehat y_v\) and \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) be the risk-band centers, and project \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) onto \([0,\widehat y_v]\), denoting the result by \(\widetilde x_{v,A}\). Coverage and \(w_R<\underline v/2\) imply \(\widehat y_v>0\). If \(x_{v,A}\le\widehat y_v\), projection onto an interval containing \(x_{v,A}\) cannot increase its error; if \(x_{v,A}>\widehat y_v\), then \(0<x_{v,A}-\widehat y_v\le y_v-\widehat y_v\le w_R\). Hence in both cases
\[
 |\widetilde x_{v,A}-x_{v,A}|\le w_R,
 \qquad |\widehat y_v-y_v|\le w_R. \tag{9}
\]
Define the feasible propagated center \(\widetilde q(v,A)=1-\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\). By (8)--(9), \(0\le\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\le1\), and therefore Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde q(v,A)-q(v,A)|
 &=\left|\frac{x_{v,A}}{y_v}-\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\right|\\
 &\le \frac{|x_{v,A}-\widetilde x_{v,A}|}{y_v}
 +\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\frac{|\widehat y_v-y_v|}{y_v}
 \le \frac{2w_R}{\underline v}. \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed singleton dependence labels, the multiplier \(1-D(v,A)/(|A|+1)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:gene-score}\) lies in \([0,1]\). An insertion changes predecessor sets only for the moved node and the nodes in its traversed block, hence for at most \(d\) nodes. Its gain is a difference of the before and after local contributions for precisely those nodes. Applying (10) to each local contribution on both sides gives the deterministic interval-propagation bound
\[
 w_S\le \frac{4d}{\underline v}w_R. \tag{11}
\]
Thus no continuity of the independence indicator has been used: (11) applies only after the separated decision has fixed every relevant indicator.

We now prove the confidence-set assertion, which does not use a width inequality. Suppose \((G_0,f,p_N,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and each HSIC coordinate queried by the exact population execution lies in \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\). On the simultaneous-coverage event, a true value \(H=0\) makes the intersected HSIC interval contain \(0\), so the set-valued rule includes the label \(\mathrm{ind}\); a true value \(H\ge\lambda\) makes that intersection meet \([\lambda,\infty)\), so the rule includes \(\mathrm{dep}\). Thus every true population dependence label is among the retained labels, regardless of \(w_H\). Likewise, every true risk lies in its interval. Honest interval extension through Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) therefore retains every true \(q(v,A)\) and every true insertion gain; if a denominator interval meets zero, the valid extension is enlarged to the known range \([0,1]\), so the true value is still retained. It follows that the exact population execution is one of the executions compatible with the bands. Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\) says that this execution terminates at \(G_0\). Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) takes the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, and hence contains \(G_0\). Since the coverage event has probability at least \(1-\alpha\),
\[
 \Pr_P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha. \tag{12}
\]

For singleton recovery, continue on the coverage event and assume \(2w_H<\lambda\). If \(H=0\), its nonnegative interval has upper endpoint at most \(2w_H<\lambda\); if \(H\ge\lambda\), its lower endpoint is at least \(H-2w_H>0\). Thus Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) returns the correct singleton label for every queried dependence indicator. If also \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies at each non-topological order a correcting insertion with true gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and the gain band makes that insertion positive for every compatible score table. Strict score ascent cannot revisit an element of the finite set \(\mathfrak S_I\), so every compatible terminal order is topological. The singleton pruning labels coincide with the population labels used by Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\). That theorem therefore gives \(G_0\) for every compatible terminal path, and taking their union proves
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}. \tag{13}
\]

It remains to verify the direct margins and the displayed sample-size order. Choose
\[
 K_1\ge \frac{8K_R}{\underline v},
 \qquad K_2\ge2K_H, \tag{14}
\]
enlarging them to absorb fixed regularity and fold constants. Since \(d\ge2\) and \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\le1\), the first direct inequality together with (5) and (14) implies \(w_R<\underline v/2\); equations (5), (11), and (14) then imply \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\). Equations (7) and (14) show that the second direct inequality implies \(2w_H<\lambda\). Thus (13) follows under the two direct inequalities.

Finally fix the regularity constants and suppose \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\lambda\le1\). Put
\[
 \gamma_d=\max\left\{2,\frac{d+5}{6}\right\},
 \qquad \beta_d=\frac{d+5}{3}.
\]
Because \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d\le1\), taking \(t_n\) no larger than a sufficiently small constant multiple of \((\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d)^{\gamma_d}\) controls both terms in the first direct inequality. Because \(\beta_d>2\) for \(d\ge2\), taking \(t_n\) no larger than a sufficiently small constant multiple of \(\lambda^{\beta_d}\) controls both terms in the second. Hence it is sufficient that
\[
 n\ge K\log(M_d/\alpha)
 \max\left\{
 \left(\frac d{\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}}\right)^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},
 \lambda^{-(d+5)/3}
 \right\}. \tag{15}
\]
The score-margin exponent equals two through \(d=7\), the two powers coincide at \(d=7\), and the nonparametric power \((d+5)/6\) governs for \(d>7\). Equation (15) is a sufficient consequence of the proved bands and is not asserted to be minimax optimal.

Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs. This is precisely the set-valued conclusion of Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\), and it completes the proof.

 K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},
 \qquad

\]

 \right\}.
\]
The score-margin exponent is \(2\) for \(d\le7\), the two powers agree at \(d=7\), and \((d+5)/6\) governs for \(d>7\); this is a sufficient-rate elbow, with no minimax claim.
